newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Little chance for change in US Cuban policy - Carter.
newsitem.headline: Little chance for change in US Cuban policy - Carter.

text.p: Former U.S. President Jimmy Carter said on Saturday he saw little chance for a rapproachment between the United States and Cuba during a second Clinton administration, given the recent stances taken by both countries.

Carter, who concluded a four-nation tour of Latin America with a meeting with Jamaican Prime Minister P.J. Patterson on Saturday, said the United States' embargo continues to play into the Cuban government's hands.

"It makes (Cuban President) Fidel Castro look like a David fighting a Goliath," Carter said. He also sharply criticised the Helms-Burton Act which seeks to tighten the embargo, calling it "one of the worst mistakes my country has ever made" and "an obstruction to moves to democratization" in Cuba.
Carter added that U.S. President Bill Clinton's decision to delay implementing part of the act demonstrates "he is trying to be flexible."

He said his Atlanta-based Carter Centre was "eager" to assist Castro should he decide to make any "innovative moves towards democracy," but added the Cuban leader has shown little interest in doing so.

Carter went to Chile, Argentina and Brazil in preparation for a Carter Centre-sponsored conference in April on "The 21st century agenda for the Americas." A number of leaders from the hemisphere were expected to attend.

His meeting with Patterson touched on a number of trade matters, arising from the Miami summit of the Americas in 1994, as well as stalled efforts to enlarge the North American Free Trade Agreement to include Chile and other countries.
Carter said he will report his findings to Clinton and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright next week.
